study type: Secondary analysis of an observational study
exposure: Early-term birth (37(0)-38(6) weeks) after confirmed fetal lung maturity
outcome: Prolonged neonatal intensive care unit stay (>2 days)
cohort: 115,502 women in 25 hospitals in the United States from 2008 through 2011, with singleton nonanomalous births at 37-40 weeks and no identifiable indication for delivery
finding: Early-term birth, even with confirmed pulmonary maturity and in the absence of medical or obstetric indications, is associated with worse neonatal respiratory and hepatic outcomes compared with full-term birth.
